text:
alex: PAGER — APAC->EU requests spiking 502/timeout after today's blue/green flip. Alerting dashboards show a sharp error-rate bump at 11:02 UTC. Deploy ID D-20240321-525. Anyone oncall?

pagerduty-bot: Paging: SRE on-call (sre-oncall) — high error rate in production (APAC -> EU routing).

sre-oncall: on it. pulling logs and route table. can someone paste the deploy link?

deploy-bot: Deploy D-20240321-525 to region=eu-west completed at 11:01:47 UTC. rollout=blue->green (50% shifted).

maya: seeing mixed origin sets in edge logs. some clients still hitting the old green pool IPs while most are on blue. errors from old pool: 502 (upstream timeout) + 403 auth mismatch in a subset.

alex: hmm. TTL was supposed to be 60s for the canary, but I see zones with 300s still. could be slow DNS propagation + long-lived connections.

maya: verified with dig across cortex:```
dig +short @8.8.8.8 canary.redwood-infer.example.com
#-> 3.210.45.12  (apac-edge-old)
#-> 52.16.22.33  (eu-edge-new)
```

alex: yep inconsistent record sets across resolvers. some ISP resolvers honoring old records. that explains partial traffic to old pool.

support-lead: we already have a few customer reports from APAC — customers complaining timeouts in generation. estimation: ~2% of requests failing, concentrated APAC->EU path.

sre-oncall: immediate plan: 1) enable feature-flag kill-switch to stop route shift 2) lower DNS TTLs to 30s (where possible) 3) purge edge caches and NLB connection draining where old pool still has steady connections.

devops: starting kill-switch now. API:```
POST https://internal-console/api/flags/kill
Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
{ "flag": "bluegreen-route", "action": "hold" }
```

devops: flag API returned 200. rollout hold engaged. stop further traffic shift.

runbook-bot: Runbook step 3: To force clients off old IPs, trigger NLB connection drain:```
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:... --attributes Key=stickiness.enabled,Value=false Key=deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds,Value=30
```

maya: running conn-drain on targets in apac-old-pool. note: persistent clients with long DNS caching will still retry existing socket until closed.

alex: lowering DNS TTL on canary zone to 30s now (propagation depends on upstream resolvers).

devops: TTL patch pushed to zones. change set id Z-2345. expecting caches to expire within ~max current-TTL (some are 300s).

sre-oncall: starting gradual rollback of the green->blue shift to bring traffic back to the stable pool while we investigate auth mismatch. executing route-control revert:```
# revert weight to 0% for green
curl -X POST https://router-control/api/rollout -d '{"deploy":"D-20240321-525","weight":0}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
```

devops: router-control accepted, weight now 0%. traffic directed to stable (old) pool.

alex: after rollback error rate dropping. dashboard shows error spike lasting ~17 minutes from first alert to rollback completion.

tim (customer): we noticed requests timing out around 11:05-11:20 UTC. thanks for the quick response. affected a handful of teams.

support-lead: created ticket for impacted customers and sent a status update. will follow up with CS for a post-incident note.

maya: root-cause hypothesis: partial DNS set still pointing at new pool IPs due to mis-ordered zone update, plus a config mismatch on auth header validation in new green pool (missing a header rewrite rule). combination caused upstream 403 + timeouts.

alex: agree. looks like deploy pipeline applied firewall/auth rule change to green targets but didn't finish a config step before traffic was shifted.

devops: action items while we remain in hold: 1) validate auth header rewrite in green pool 2) run canary traffic to validated targets with healthchecks 3) audit zone update ordering in deploy pipeline 4) generate customer impact summary.

sre-oncall: measuring impact: peak error rate + latency spike from 11:02 to 11:19 UTC. estimate ~2.1% of global requests impacted, concentrated in APAC (roughly 5% of APAC traffic). incident severity set to Sev2.

runbook-bot: Post-incident tasks created: INCIDENT-4882 (config fix), INCIDENT-4883 (deploy pipeline ordering), INCIDENT-4884 (dns-ttl-default-check).

support-lead: coordinating with customer success for follow-up. internal comms draft ready for review.

maya: redeploying config fix to green pool behind a manual cutover, running healthchecks:```
# check auth header passthrough
curl -I -H 'X-Auth: test' https://green-edge.test/health
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```

devops: validated, auth header rewrite present. performing controlled 5% canary to green with strict health probes and monitoring.

alex: monitoring windows show no errors after config fix. if stable for 15m, we'll retry gradual rollout with shorter TTL orchestration and preflight health checks.

sre-oncall: marking incident as mitigated. rollback completed and kill-switch held. prepping postmortem.

support-lead: sent customer update: brief incident summary, affected window 11:02-11:19 UTC, mitigation actions and next steps.

alex: thumbs up. postmortem owners: maya (config fix), devops (deploy pipeline), alex (operational). target publish in 48hrs.

tim (customer): appreciate the quick updates — will watch for the postmortem.

sre-oncall: closing the page. I'll create timeline + attach traces to INCIDENT-4882.

alex: thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

# reactions: :rotating_light: on initial alert, :white_check_mark: on mitigation, :memo: for postmortem follow-up
